key_insight: RFM is a lightweight retinal foundation model that, when kept frozen and paired with simple linear heads, generalises well across eye disease grading, biomarker prediction, and future cardiovascular/neurologic risk tasks.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a single retinal image encoder could support multiple screening and risk-stratification applications without task-specific retraining, potentially simplifying deployment in ophthalmic and broader multimodal AI systems.
method: Domain-adapted using the LeJEPA self-supervised objective plus retinal pretext tasks
Evaluated with one frozen backbone and a linear head across external classification and regression benchmarks
evidence_signal: The model was trained on 4.3 million colour fundus photographs and tested on six external datasets covering seven regression phenotypes and eight classification benchmarks, including 3-year incident myocardial infarction, stroke, and Parkinson’s disease.
watch_item: Results were strongest under frozen-encoder evaluation and the Parkinson’s endpoint had only 11 cases, so broader clinical validation and larger prospective studies are needed before deployment.
paper_title: RFM: A Lightweight Retinal Foundation Model for Generalised Oculomics
